history.dynasty: None (ancient shrine; later within Akbar's 1583 fort)
history.period: Ancient - described by Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang in 644 AD; underground gallery; lighting installed 1906
history.summary: Patalpuri is the ancient underground temple inside Allahabad Fort (built by Akbar in 1583), accessed by stairs descending from the fort's eastern side. Its heart is the Akshayavat, the 'immortal' banyan whose roots emerge from the stone floor - described by Hiuen Tsang in 644 AD when the temple stood on a high mound with a courtyard, and associated with Rama and Sita's meditation, sage Markandeya and the Pandavas (Puranic/epic tradition, verify). The subterranean gallery is roofed with ash-coloured stone slabs ~1.97 m above the floor on 84 pillars (seven rows of 12), with medieval sculptures, mostly relocated from other temples. Electric lighting was installed in 1906 and an easier 25.6 m passage replaced the old narrow path. ACCESS RESTRICTION FLAG: the fort is an Indian Army Ordnance Depot / high-security zone; entry needs a valid photo ID, security check and sometimes prior permission from the Fort Commandant; a separate corridor entrance from the Sangam side near Bade Hanuman Temple (~500 m) now avoids the army area. CSV TOWN FLAG: CSV town 'Allahabad' - the city was officially renamed Prayagraj in 2018; documented as Prayagraj.

name: Patalpuri Temple
town_description: Prayagraj (formerly Allahabad) is the sacred city at the Triveni Sangam - the confluence of the Ganga, Yamuna and mythical Saraswati - and the site of the Kumbh and Magh Melas. It is a major Hindu pilgrimage centre as well as a historic city with the Mughal-era Allahabad Fort, Anand Bhavan and Prayagraj University.
tradition: Hinduism (mixed - Shaiva, Vaishnava and Shakta idols; Akshayavat veneration)

travel.road: Inside Allahabad Fort on the Yamuna bank near Sangam; use the separate corridor entrance from the Sangam side near Bade Hanuman Temple (~500 m away); carry valid photo ID (Aadhaar/Voter ID/Passport)
